meta.purpose: Human- and LLM-readable decoding of the abbreviated cortical region labels used in human_data.json. Given a natural-language user query (e.g. 'the area for face recognition' or 'where is movement controlled'), an LLM can match against the 'description'/'keywords' fields here and narrow down to the actual abbreviation label, then prepend 'L_' (left) or 'R_' (right) to address a specific hemisphere.
meta.atlas: HCP-MMP1.0 multi-modal parcellation (Glasser MF et al. 2016, Nature 536:171-178), 180 areas per hemisphere. Region short names and full names follow that parcellation; areas are grouped into the 22 cortical 'sections' defined in the same work.
meta.label_convention: Region labels in human_data.json are prefixed 'L_' (left) or 'R_' (right); strip the prefix to look up the base abbreviation below. The two hemispheres share the same 180 base abbreviations.
meta.species_note: Coordinates and areas describe the human cortex in ICBM/MNI-2009c space. Functional roles are the well-established human functions of each area where known; for a minority of areas with limited functional characterisation the description is grounded in the area's 22-section membership rather than a specific claim.
meta.confidence_notes: full_name, lobe and the 22-section 'group' are taken verbatim from the Glasser 2016 final table (HCP-MMP1_UniqueRegionList.csv). The 'description' and 'keywords' are a curated interpretive layer: specific for well-characterised areas (e.g. V1, MT, A1, 4/3b, 44/45, hippocampus), and section-grounded generic text for the rest. Verify against primary sources for critical work.
sources: Glasser MF, Coalson TS, Robinson EC, et al. 2016. A multi-modal parcellation of human cerebral cortex. Nature 536:171-178 (+ Supplementary Neuroanatomical Results).
HCP-MMP1_UniqueRegionList.csv (Glasser 2016 final table; region names, lobe, 22 cortical sections). https://bitbucket.org/dpat/tools/raw/master/REF/ATLASES/HCP-MMP1_UniqueRegionList.csv

groups.V1: Primary visual cortex — the first cortical stage of vision (V1), where signals from the eyes first arrive.
groups.EVIS: Early visual cortex — early retinotopic areas that process basic form, colour and motion just after V1.
groups.DSV: Dorsal-stream visual cortex — the dorsal 'where/how' visual stream for spatial location, motion and visually guided action.
groups.VSV: Ventral-stream visual cortex — the ventral 'what' visual stream for recognising objects, faces, places and colour.
groups.MT+: MT+ complex and neighbouring visual areas — the MT+ motion complex that analyses visual motion and moving objects.
groups.SM: Somatosensory and motor cortex — primary sensorimotor cortex around the central sulcus for touch and voluntary movement.
groups.PCMC: Paracentral lobular and mid-cingulate cortex — medial sensorimotor and mid-cingulate cortex linking body/limb representation to action.
groups.PM: Premotor cortex — premotor cortex that plans and prepares movements, including eye movements.
groups.POP: Posterior opercular cortex — opercular cortex around the Sylvian fissure for secondary somatosensory, taste and vestibular processing.
groups.EAUD: Early auditory cortex — primary and early auditory cortex (core and belt) for basic sound processing.
groups.AAUD: Auditory association cortex — higher auditory and superior-temporal cortex for complex sounds, voices and speech.
groups.IFOP: Insular and frontal opercular cortex — insula and frontal operculum for interoception, taste, smell and visceral-emotional processing.
groups.MTMP: Medial temporal cortex — medial temporal / hippocampal-formation cortex for memory, navigation and scene processing.
groups.LTMP: Lateral temporal cortex — lateral and anterior temporal cortex for high-level object/face vision and semantic knowledge.
groups.TPOJ: Temporo-parieto-occipital junction — the temporo-parieto-occipital junction for multisensory integration and social perception.
groups.SPAR: Superior parietal cortex — superior parietal and intraparietal cortex for spatial attention, reaching and grasping.
groups.IPAR: Inferior parietal cortex — inferior parietal cortex (angular/supramarginal gyri) for attention, language and action understanding.
groups.PCIN: Posterior cingulate cortex — posterior cingulate, precuneus and retrosplenial cortex for memory, navigation and default-mode/self-referential processing.
groups.ACMP: Anterior cingulate and medial prefrontal cortex — anterior cingulate and medial prefrontal cortex for emotion, motivation, conflict monitoring and autonomic control.
groups.OPF: Orbital and polar frontal cortex — orbitofrontal and frontopolar cortex for reward valuation, decision-making and abstract goal representation.
groups.IFC: Inferior frontal cortex — inferior frontal cortex, including the language/Broca region, for speech, cognitive control and response inhibition.
groups.DLPFC: Dorsolateral prefrontal cortex — dorsolateral prefrontal cortex for working memory, executive control and attention.

V1.description: Primary (striate) visual cortex. The first cortical stage of vision, mapping the visual field retinotopically and extracting edges, orientation and contrast.

MST.description: Medial superior temporal area. Processes wide-field/complex motion (optic flow) for self-motion perception and smooth-pursuit eye movements.

V6.description: Sixth visual area. Medial dorsal-stream area encoding wide-field/self-motion (optic flow) and spatial layout for reaching.

V2.description: Second visual area. Early extrastriate cortex processing contours, texture, figure-ground segregation and combinations of orientation and colour.

V3.description: Third visual area. Early visual cortex contributing to form and coherent-motion processing.

V4.description: Fourth visual area. A key colour-processing area that also represents shape and curvature for object vision.

V8.description: Eighth visual area. Ventral occipital area involved in colour perception.

4.description: Primary motor cortex (M1). Directly drives voluntary movement, sending commands to the muscles; somatotopically mapped (the motor homunculus).

3b.description: Area 3b — the core of primary somatosensory cortex (S1) for fine touch, mapped somatotopically (sensory homunculus).

FEF.description: Frontal eye fields — controls voluntary eye movements (saccades) and shifts of visual spatial attention.

PEF.description: Premotor eye field — frontal area contributing to eye-movement control and visual attention.

55b.description: Area 55b — lateral frontal area implicated in language (speech) and eye movements.

V3A.description: Dorsal visual area V3A, sensitive to visual motion and the position of moving objects.

RSC.description: Retrosplenial complex — central to spatial navigation, translating between viewpoint- and map-based spatial frames; scene memory.

POS2.description: Parieto-occipital sulcus area 2 — medial parietal cortex for spatial and scene processing.

V7.description: Seventh visual area, a dorsal area involved in spatial attention and motion.

IPS1.description: Intraparietal sulcus area 1. Retinotopic parietal area for spatial attention and eye-movement planning.

FFC.description: Fusiform face complex. The classic 'fusiform face area' (FFA), specialised for recognising faces and other expert visual categories.

V3B.description: Dorsal extrastriate area V3B, processing motion and form.

LO1.description: Lateral occipital area 1. Object-selective lateral occipital cortex for shape and object recognition.

LO2.description: Lateral occipital area 2. Object-selective lateral occipital cortex for shape and object recognition.

PIT.description: Posterior inferotemporal complex — a ventral-stream area for recognising objects and shapes.

MT.description: Middle temporal area (V5/MT). The core motion area, essential for perceiving the speed and direction of visual motion.

A1.description: Primary auditory cortex (A1). The first cortical stage of hearing; tonotopically mapped by sound frequency (pitch).

PSL.description: Perisylvian language area — posterior perisylvian cortex involved in language processing.

SFL.description: Superior frontal language area — superior frontal cortex contributing to language and cognitive control.

PCV.description: Precuneus visual area — precuneus cortex for visuospatial imagery, navigation and default-mode processing.

STV.description: Superior temporal visual area — temporoparietal cortex for multisensory, visual-motion and social processing.

7Pm.description: Medial area 7P — superior parietal cortex for spatial attention, reaching and visuomotor coordination.

7m.description: Area 7m — medial parietal / precuneus cortex for visuospatial imagery, navigation and default-mode processing.

POS1.description: Parieto-occipital sulcus area 1 — medial parietal cortex for spatial and scene processing.
